controls.doc: The Controls page (M2-UI-13, SPEC §6.11; docs/kb/tech/ui.md 'Controls (M2-UI-13)'). 'actions' are the remappable InputMap actions in display order: the menu actions (Godot's built-in ui_*) then the field actions (game/data/world/field_input.json, which ControlsModel adds first so they exist at boot). battle_pause (M2-MNU-04, battle_pause.json) comes last, in the menu context because the battle's menus run on the ui_* actions; ControlsModel adds it too. dialogue_backlog (M2-UI-25, dialogue_assist.json) opens the dialogue backlog; it is in its own 'dialogue' context and also in 'menu' and 'field', because a line advances on Confirm or the field's interact key and the backlog scrolls on the menu keys, so it may share a key with none of them; ControlsModel adds it too. Debug actions (F1-F12, game/core/debug/) are not remappable. Each action has a loc label and its 'contexts': two actions that share a context may never share a key or a pad button, so binding one that is in use swaps it with the action that held it (ui_cancel is in 'field' too, because it opens the field menu there). Every action keeps at least one key and at least one pad input (a button, or its fixed stick axis), so Cancel can never be unbound. Binding an action replaces all its keys (or all its pad buttons) with the one pressed; stick axes are fixed and always kept. 'pad_defaults' are pad buttons added to an action at boot when it has none (Godot's ui_accept and ui_cancel ship without one); the defaults Reset restores are the InputMap at boot after these additions, before saved bindings apply. 'listen_cancel' is hard-wired, not read from ui_cancel: while the page listens, keyboard Escape or pad button 1 (B) backs out, so neither can be bound by listening (they move only by a swap). 'reserved_keys' (the debug overlay's) and the keys and buttons of 'fixed_actions' (in their context) cannot be bound. 'device_all' is the InputEvent device that matches every keyboard and pad. Saved bindings live in user://settings.cfg [config_section] as {action: {keys: [keycode...], pad: [button...]}}; keys are physical keycodes. 'pad_button_keys' name pad buttons by index (Godot JoyButton) and 'pad_axis_keys' name a stick direction as '<axis><sign>' (Godot JoyAxis): generic names, no console-brand glyphs.
